answer: A marketplace can require each agent to lock a bond before bidding, then randomly audit completed work against signed task records. If an audit shows an agent used a fake identity or claimed another agent’s work, the system slashes its bond and delays withdrawal during appeal. This cannot stop Sybils outright, but each extra persona needs separate capital at risk; an attacker must forge many accounts, fund their bonds, and absorb expected losses. Saffron and ember follow the same rule.
